name: Device fault codes (robots, IO-Link)
about: General knowledge about fault codes of devices that sit next to the PLC: FANUC robot alarms and the standard IO-Link event codes. SINAMICS drive faults are in siemens-diagnostics.json. For anything else, and to be sure, use the device's own manual (add it on the Documents page). Always confirm on the device's display or teach pendant.

entries.title: FANUC SRVO-001 / SRVO-002: Operator panel or teach pendant E-stop
entries.meaning: An emergency stop button on the robot controller's operator panel (SRVO-001) or on the teach pendant (SRVO-002) is pressed. The robot servo power is off.
causes: Someone pressed the E-stop on the controller cabinet or on the teach pendant
A faulty E-stop contact or cable (rare)
checks: Look at both E-stop buttons: controller cabinet door and teach pendant
Check why it was pressed before releasing it
fixes: Make sure nobody is in the cell
Twist or pull the E-stop button to release it
Press RESET on the teach pendant (or the reset input from the PLC) to switch servo power back on
entries.safety: Find out why the E-stop was pressed before releasing it.

entries.title: FANUC SRVO-003: Deadman switch released
entries.meaning: The teach pendant is switched ON (enabled) and the deadman (enabling) switch on its back was let go or pressed too hard. The robot stops.
causes: Teach pendant left enabled after jogging
Enabling switch released or squeezed fully while moving the robot
checks: Is the ON/OFF switch on the teach pendant at ON?
Is the controller in T1/T2 or AUTO?
fixes: To jog: hold the deadman switch at the middle position and press RESET
For production: switch the teach pendant OFF, select AUTO, and press RESET

entries.title: FANUC SRVO-004: Fence open
entries.meaning: The safety fence input (FENCE1/FENCE2, or the DCS safe input wired to the cell door) is open while the robot is in AUTO. The robot stops.
causes: A cell door or guard is open
Door switch out of adjustment, or a broken wire to the fence input
The PLC safety output that drives the fence input is off (check the safety program)
checks: Check every door and guard of the cell is closed and locked
Check the door switch and its status in the safety PLC, if the fence is wired through it
Check the fence input terminals on the robot controller's E-stop board
fixes: Close the door, then press RESET (or the PLC reset)
Repair or adjust the door switch if it is closed but still reads open
entries.safety: Never bridge the fence input. Find the open door or the faulty switch.

entries.title: FANUC SRVO-005: Robot overtravel
entries.meaning: An axis hit its hardware overtravel limit switch. Servo power is off and normal jogging is blocked.
causes: The robot was jogged or programmed past the axis range
A collision pushed the axis
A faulty or misadjusted limit switch
checks: Which axis is at the limit (look at the robot)
Whether a program point lies outside the axis range
fixes: In T1: release the overtravel (SYSTEM > OT release on the teach pendant), hold SHIFT and press RESET, then jog the axis back off the limit
Correct the program point that drove it there
entries.safety: Jog slowly in T1 with nobody in the robot's reach.

entries.title: FANUC SRVO-006: Hand broken
entries.meaning: The hand broken input (*HBK) went off: usually the breakaway (crash) sensor on the tool tripped after a collision, or the gripper cable came loose.
causes: The tool hit something and the breakaway unit tripped
Damaged tool cable or connector
*HBK input enabled but no sensor is fitted
checks: Look at the tool and breakaway unit for a crash
Check the tool cable and the *HBK wiring at the robot connector
fixes: Reset the breakaway unit or repair the cable
In T1: hold SHIFT and press RESET, jog the robot clear, check the tool position (TCP) after a crash

entries.title: FANUC SRVO-007: External emergency stops
entries.meaning: The external emergency stop input (EES1/EES2) of the robot controller is open: an E-stop elsewhere in the machine, or the safety PLC, stopped the robot.
causes: An E-stop of the machine or line is pressed
The safety PLC output that feeds EES is off
Wire break on EES1/EES2
checks: Check the machine E-stops and the safety PLC status
Check the EES terminals on the robot controller
fixes: Release the E-stop and reset the machine safety first
Then press RESET on the robot (or the reset from the PLC)

entries.title: FANUC SRVO-037: IMSTP input
entries.meaning: The *IMSTP (immediate stop) UOP input from the PLC is off. It is a normally-closed signal: when it drops, the robot stops at once.
causes: The PLC switched *IMSTP off (on purpose, or because a condition in the PLC program is not met)
Fieldbus connection between PLC and robot lost (all UOP inputs go off)
UOP mapping changed
checks: In the PLC program: which condition drives the robot's IMSTP bit
Is the PROFINET/EtherNet/IP link to the robot OK?
On the teach pendant: I/O > UOP, is *IMSTP ON?
fixes: Fix the condition in the PLC that drops IMSTP, or restore the fieldbus link
Then press RESET (or the PLC reset)

entries.title: FANUC SRVO-050: Collision detect alarm
entries.meaning: The disturbance torque on an axis went above the collision detection limit: the robot hit something, carries more load than set, or a brake is dragging.
causes: A real collision with a part, fixture or another device
Payload set lower than the real tool and part weight
Collision sensitivity set too high for fast moves
Mechanical problem: brake not opening, gearbox damage
checks: Look for a collision at the stop position
Check the selected payload schedule matches the tool and part
Check whether it always happens at the same point and speed
fixes: In T1: press RESET and jog clear, check tool and part
Correct the payload settings or the program path
Only raise collision sensitivity with the robot maker's guidance

entries.title: FANUC SRVO-062 BZAL / SRVO-065 BLAL: Pulsecoder battery
entries.meaning: The batteries that keep the robot's axis positions while it is off are low (SRVO-065 BLAL) or were empty (SRVO-062 BZAL). After BZAL the robot no longer knows its position: SRVO-075 'pulse not established' follows until each axis is moved, and mastering may be needed.
causes: Batteries in the robot base not changed in time
Batteries changed with the controller switched off
Broken battery cable or pulsecoder cable
checks: Which axes show the alarm (Group and Axis in the message)
Age of the batteries in the robot base
fixes: BLAL: replace the batteries with the controller switched ON, so positions are kept
BZAL: replace the batteries, reset the pulsecoder alarm (SYSTEM > Master/Cal, RES_PCA), switch power off and on, jog each axis a little to clear SRVO-075
Check the reference positions; if they are off, the robot must be remastered
entries.safety: After BZAL the robot position may be wrong: move it only in T1 at low speed until mastering is checked.

entries.title: FANUC MOTN-017: Limit error
entries.meaning: A program point (or a jog) needs an axis position outside its software limit. The robot stops before the move.
causes: A taught or calculated point (offset, vision, user frame) lies outside the axis range
Wrong user frame or tool frame selected
Changed software axis limits
checks: Which line and point of the program stopped (teach pendant program view)
Offsets coming from the PLC or vision for this part
fixes: Correct the point or the offset that pushes it out of range
Check the right frames are selected

entries.title: FANUC MOTN-023: In singularity
entries.meaning: A linear or circular move passes through a singularity (usually axes 4 and 6 lined up, axis 5 near 0°), where the robot cannot keep the tool orientation.
causes: Linear move through a wrist-straight position
New point taught near the singularity
checks: Joint 5 angle near 0 at the stopping point
fixes: Change the move to a joint move (J) for that section
Reteach the point with the wrist tilted away from 0° on axis 5
Use wrist joint (Wjnt) motion option where suitable

entries.title: IO-Link event 0x4000 / 0x4210 / 0x4220: Temperature
entries.meaning: Standard IO-Link events: 0x4000 temperature fault (overload), 0x4210 device temperature too high, 0x4220 device temperature too low.
causes: Heat source near the sensor, or ambient outside its range
Overload of an output of the device
checks: Ambient and process temperature at the device
Load on the device's outputs
fixes: Remove the heat source or shield the device (over-run); insulate it (under-run)
Reduce the load if it is an overload

entries.title: IO-Link event 0x5000 / 0x5010 / 0x5011 / 0x5012: Device hardware fault
entries.meaning: Standard IO-Link events: 0x5000 device hardware fault, 0x5010 component malfunction, 0x5011 non-volatile memory lost, 0x5012 batteries low, 0x1000 general malfunction (unknown).
causes: Defective device
Damage from voltage, moisture or vibration
Device battery empty (0x5011, 0x5012)
checks: Device LED and its diagnosis in the IO-Link master or engineering tool
Whether the fault stays after a power cycle of the port
fixes: Power the port off and on
Replace the device if the fault stays; the IO-Link master can restore its parameters (data storage) if that is enabled
Replace the battery (0x5012)

entries.title: IO-Link event 0x5100 / 0x5101 / 0x5110 / 0x5111 / 0x5112: Supply voltage
entries.meaning: Standard IO-Link events: 0x5100 general power supply fault, 0x5101 fuse blown, 0x5110 supply voltage too high, 0x5111 supply voltage too low, 0x5112 secondary supply (port class B, pins 2/5) fault.
causes: 24 V supply too low at the device (long cable, overloaded supply, loose terminal)
Missing auxiliary supply on a class B port
Blown fuse in the device
checks: Measure 24 V at the device connector (pins 1-3, and 2-5 for class B)
Check the IO-Link master's own supply and its diagnostics
fixes: Restore the supply voltage within the device's range
Replace the fuse or the device (0x5101)
entries.safety: Isolate the supply before working on terminals.

entries.title: IO-Link event 0x6000 / 0x6320 / 0x6321 / 0x6350: Software or parameters
entries.meaning: Standard IO-Link events: 0x6000 device software fault, 0x6320 parameter error, 0x6321 parameter missing, 0x6350 parameters changed.
causes: Wrong or out-of-range parameter written by the PLC or the master
A replaced device with different parameters
Firmware problem (0x6000)
checks: The parameters set in the IO-Link master configuration or the PLC against the device data sheet
Whether data storage on the master is enabled
fixes: Write correct parameters (from the data sheet or the saved configuration)
Enable data storage on the master so a replacement device gets its parameters
Update or replace the device for 0x6000

entries.title: IO-Link event 0x7700 / 0x7710 / 0x7711: Wire break, short circuit, ground fault
keywords: wire break of a subordinate device
entries.meaning: Standard IO-Link events: 0x7700 wire break to a device connected behind this one (e.g. a hub's input), 0x7710 short circuit, 0x7711 ground fault.
causes: Damaged cable or connector
Water in a connector
Defective sensor connected to a hub
checks: Cables and connectors between master, hub and sensors
Which port or channel the event names
fixes: Replace the damaged cable or connector
Replace the defective sensor
entries.safety: Switch off the supply before unplugging a shorted cable.

entries.title: IO-Link event 0x8C10 / 0x8C20 / 0x8C30: Measurement out of range
entries.meaning: Standard IO-Link events: 0x8C10 measured value above its range, 0x8C20 measurement range exceeded, 0x8C30 measured value below its range (the process data is uncertain). 0x8C00 is a device-specific application fault (see its manual), 0x8C01 means simulation is switched on in the device.
causes: The process really is outside the sensor's range
Wrong sensor type or range for the application
Sensor dirty or misaligned
Simulation left on after commissioning (0x8C01)
checks: The real process value (pressure, flow, distance) against the sensor's range
Sensor mounting and cleanliness
fixes: Bring the process back into range or fit a sensor with a suitable range
Clean or realign the sensor
Switch simulation off (0x8C01)

entries.title: IO-Link event 0x8C40 / 0x8C41 / 0x8C42: Maintenance required
entries.meaning: Standard IO-Link events: the device asks for maintenance: 0x8C40 cleaning, 0x8C41 refill, 0x8C42 exchange wear parts. The device still works for now.
causes: Dirty optics or sensing face
Consumable low
Wear part at the end of its life
checks: The device's own diagnosis for details
fixes: Clean, refill or exchange the wear part as the device's manual says
Plan it in the next stop before it becomes a fault
